capture.final_message:
Prove the outer conjunction independently.

For the measure statement, use a Hahn-style witness for \(\mu \perp \nu_2\): choose a measurable set \(S\) such that \(\mu(S^{c})=0\) and \(\nu_2(S)=0\). If \(\nu_1(A)=0\), then \((\nu_1+\nu_2)(A\cap S)=0\), so absolute continuity gives \(\mu(A\cap S)=0\); the part \(A\cap S^{c}\) is \(\mu\)-null by construction. Hence \(\mu(A)=0\), proving \(\mu\ll\nu_1\).

For the equivalence, observe that both universally quantified assertions hold independently:

- The antidiagonal of the single-supported finsupp \(n[a]\) consists exactly of pairs \((i[a],j[a])\) with \(i+j=n\). Establish this by Finset extensionality, using coordinatewise equality and the injectivity of `Finsupp.single a`; this identifies it with the mapped natural-number antidiagonal.
- If \(s\) and \(t\) are disjoint, then \(u\cap s\subseteq s\), so disjointness is preserved by shrinking the left-hand set.

Thus each implication of the `Iff` can simply discard its premise and invoke the corresponding unconditional fact.
